---

Every entry record the front end receives carries its derived status.

`Entries()` reports one record per entry, newest first, since an identifier opens with the moment the
graph received it. A record holds what the frontmatter carries: the type, the layer, the kind, the
confidence, the participants, the topics, the summary, and the body. It also holds the
status, and names the live entry that closed or superseded a retired one.

Status belongs in the first version rather than a later one. A reader who cannot tell a retired
decision from a live one meets the failure this viewer exists to prevent. A table without status
looks authoritative and is not.

Frontmatter alone loses. It is the smallest slice that puts a real table on screen. It shows
decisions with no sign that the graph retired some of them, and it grows a second path for the
status straight afterwards.

Frontmatter first with the status arriving behind it loses as well. A large graph paints at once, and
the reader meets a moment where every row's status is unknown, which misleads the same way.

The accepted cost is a parser of rendered output that exists before anything proves the table
consuming it. That parser names the sdd version it targets.

Nothing follows from this on its own. It fixes the shape of a record that other entries commission
work against, and a change to that shape arrives as its own decision.
